title_en: Choosing Who to Invest In: Why Your Time Should Follow Action, Not Hope
title_zh: 選擇把時間投資在誰身上：你的時間應該跟著行動走，而不是跟著希望走
excerpt_en: A leader's time is the scarcest thing in the team. Spend it on the people you hope will start, and you'll run out. Spend it on the people already moving, and the whole team speeds up.
excerpt_zh: 領袖的時間，是團隊裡最稀缺的資源。把它花在你希望會開始的人身上，你很快就會用光。把它花在已經在動的人身上，整個團隊都會加速。

title_en: The First Week Decides the First Year: What New Partners Learn by Watching You
title_zh: 第一週決定第一年：新夥伴看著你，學到了什麼
excerpt_en: New partners listen to what you say in their first week, but they copy what you do. Show them the work, let them try it beside you, and the habits they form will carry them through the year.
excerpt_zh: 新夥伴第一週會聽你說什麼，但他們複製的是你做什麼。讓他們看到工作怎麼做，讓他們在你身邊試，他們養成的習慣，會陪他們走過一整年。

title_en: Leave the Door Open: What Sun Tzu Teaches About Never Cornering People
title_zh: 留一道門：孫子教我們，永遠不要把人逼到死角
excerpt_en: "When you surround an army, leave an outlet free." Push someone into a corner and they fight back. Give them a way out and they often walk towards you on their own.
excerpt_zh: 「圍師必闕，窮寇勿迫。」把人逼到死角，他會拼命反抗。給他一條出路，他往往會自己走向你。

title_en: Following Up Without Chasing: How to Stay in Touch So People Are Glad to Hear From You
title_zh: 跟進，而不是追著跑：怎麼保持聯絡，讓對方樂於收到你的訊息
excerpt_en: Most opportunities are lost to silence rather than rejection. The fix is following up properly: often enough to be remembered, kindly enough to be welcome, and always with something worth reading.
excerpt_zh: 大多數機會不是被拒絕，而是在沉默中流失。解法是好好跟進：頻繁到對方記得你，溫和到對方歡迎你，而且每次都帶著值得一讀的東西。

title_en: You Don't Need Every Answer: The Power of a Third Voice
title_zh: 你不需要知道所有答案：第三個聲音的力量
excerpt_en: New builders often think they must be the expert before they can share anything. You don't. Your job is to connect people with the right voice, and that voice doesn't have to be yours.
excerpt_zh: 很多新人以為，自己要先成為專家，才能分享任何東西。其實不必。你的工作是把人跟對的聲音連起來，而那個聲音不一定是你。

title_en: The Real Reason You Avoid Inviting, and How to Stop Avoiding It
title_zh: 你一直逃避邀約的真正原因，以及怎麼停止逃避
excerpt_en: Most people who stop inviting don't lack skill. They are protecting themselves from a feeling. Name the feeling, shrink the stakes, and the phone gets lighter.
excerpt_zh: 大多數不再邀約的人，缺的不是技巧。他們是在保護自己，躲開某一種感覺。說出那種感覺、降低賭注，手機就會變輕。

title_en: "I Thought You Were My Friend": Why I Ask for an Opinion Before I Invite
title_zh: 「我以為你是我朋友」：為什麼我邀約之前，先請對方給意見
excerpt_en: The most painful lesson of my career came over a cup of coffee with a university friend. It changed how I open every conversation: with a question about what the other person thinks.
excerpt_zh: 我事業裡最慘痛的一課，是跟一位大學同學喝咖啡時學到的。它改變了我開啟每一段對話的方式：先問對方怎麼想。

title_en: Your Best Prospects Probably Aren't on Your Warm List
title_zh: 你最好的潛在客戶，多半不在你的熟人名單上
excerpt_en: Every new builder is told to start with friends and family. It's a fine place to start and a poor place to stay. The people most likely to value what you offer are usually people you haven't met yet.
excerpt_zh: 每個新人都被教導從親朋好友開始。這是不錯的起點，卻不是久留的地方。最可能珍惜你所提供的東西的人，通常是你還沒認識的人。

title_en: Busy for 60 Days, Zero Customers: The Seven Daily Actions That Fixed It
title_zh: 忙了60天，客戶是零：改變局面的每日七項行動
excerpt_en: He posted every day, attended every training and read every brochure. Sixty days in, he had no customers. The problem was where his hours went, and the fix was seven simple actions a day for 90 days.
excerpt_zh: 他每天發文、參加每一場培訓、讀完所有產品手冊。60天後，客戶還是零。問題出在他的時間花在哪裡，解法是每天七個簡單的動作，持續90天。

title_en: Speak From Experience, Not From the Brochure
title_zh: 用你的經驗說話，而不是用產品手冊
excerpt_en: People can tell within seconds whether you are repeating a brochure or describing your own life. Before you share any product, live with it long enough to talk about it honestly, including what didn't change for you.
excerpt_zh: 對方幾秒鐘內就分辨得出，你是在背產品手冊，還是在講自己的生活。分享任何產品之前，先跟它一起生活夠久，久到你能誠實地談它，包括在你身上沒有改變的地方。

title_en: Your Team Copies All of You, Including the Parts You'd Rather It Didn't
title_zh: 你的團隊會複製完整的你，包括你不希望他們學的那部分
excerpt_en: Duplication is the whole point of this business, and it doesn't stop at your strengths. If your team keeps attracting people and losing them, look at what you are modelling when you are not on stage.
excerpt_zh: 複製是這個事業的核心，而它不會只複製你的優勢。如果你的團隊一直吸引人、又一直留不住人，看看你不在台上的時候，示範的是什麼。

title_en: Ask Before You Sell: Your Customers Already Know Your Market
title_zh: 先問再賣：你的客戶，早就知道你的市場在哪裡
excerpt_en: Most of us guess who our customers are and why they buy. The people who already bought from you can tell you, in their own words, if you ask the right questions and then stop talking.
excerpt_zh: 我們大多是用猜的：猜客戶是誰、猜他們為什麼買。其實已經跟你買過的人，可以用他們自己的話告訴你，前提是你問對問題，然後閉上嘴。

title_en: Selling to a Generation That Hates Being Sold To: Winning Gen Z Without the Hype
title_zh: 向討厭被推銷的世代銷售：不靠炒作贏得 Z 世代
excerpt_en: Gen Z has a finely-tuned radar for everything direct selling traditionally does — hype, urgency, fake scarcity. The old playbook doesn't just fail with them; it repels them. Here's the new approach.
excerpt_zh: Z 世代對直銷的老套路有著極其敏銳的雷達：炒作、緊迫感、假稀缺。舊劇本對他們不只是失效，而是直接把他們推開。這篇談的是新做法。

title_en: Recognition That Actually Works: Beyond Pins, Trips, and Stage Walks
title_zh: 真正有效的肯定：超越別針、旅遊和台上亮相
excerpt_en: The industry loves pins, trips, and stage walks — but most recognition doesn't actually drive behavior. Here's what makes recognition work, drawn from years watching it from the corporate side.
excerpt_zh: 業界熱愛別針、旅遊和台上亮相，但大多數的肯定其實無法真正驅動行為。從企業端觀察多年後，我看懂了什麼樣的肯定才有效。

title_en: The Plateau: Why Your Income Stopped Growing — and the 3 Levers That Restart It
title_zh: 高原期：為什麼你的收入停止成長，以及重啟成長的三個槓桿
excerpt_en: You climb and climb, then flat. Same income, month after month. The plateau is the most misunderstood phase of a direct selling career — and three structural levers that restart the growth.
excerpt_zh: 你一路往上爬，然後，停了。收入月復一月停在原地。高原期是直銷生涯中最被誤解的階段，以及三個能重啟成長的結構性槓桿。

title_en: The AI Disruption: What Artificial Intelligence Really Means for Direct Selling Leaders
title_zh: AI 衝擊：人工智慧對直銷領袖的真正意義
excerpt_en: Social media was going to 'kill' direct selling. It didn't. Now it's AI. This time the panic is half-right and half-dangerously-wrong — here's what AI actually changes, and what it never will.
excerpt_zh: 當年大家說社群媒體會「殺死」直銷，結果沒有。現在輪到 AI。這一次的恐慌一半對、一半危險地錯，AI 究竟改變了什麼，又有什麼是它永遠無法取代的。

title_en: The Comeback: How to Restart When You've Lost Momentum
title_zh: 東山再起：失去動能後，如何重新開始
excerpt_en: Every long-haul leader hits a stall. The strategic anatomy of a comeback — drawn from the leaders I've coached through it. How to restart when motivation is gone.
excerpt_zh: 每個走長線的領袖都會遇到停滯期。一場真正的東山再起該長什麼樣，來自我陪伴走過的領袖。沒了動力時，如何重新開始。

title_en: What Sun Tzu Got Wrong About Modern Direct Selling
title_zh: 在現代直銷裡，孫子兵法錯在哪裡
excerpt_en: I wrote a book about applying Sun Tzu to direct selling. Here's the contrarian take: where the 2,500-year-old playbook still works, where modern terrain breaks it, and why both matter.
excerpt_zh: 我寫了一本把孫子兵法應用到直銷的書。這篇給你逆向思考：2500 年的兵書哪些原則仍適用，哪些已被現代戰場推翻，為什麼兩面都要看。

title_en: The Two-Year Wall: Why Half Your Team Quits in Year Two
title_zh: 兩年之牆：為什麼一半的團隊會在第二年放棄
excerpt_en: Year 1 is excitement. Year 3 is momentum. Year 2 is the wall. Why this specific year tests retention, what corporate data shows, and how to coach your team through it.
excerpt_zh: 第一年靠熱情。第三年靠慣性。第二年，是一道牆。為什麼這一年最考驗留存率，企業端的數據說了什麼，以及該怎麼帶你的人走過去。

title_en: Leadership During Company Transitions: How to Move Without Losing Your Tribe
title_zh: 公司轉換期的領導：如何不失去你一手帶起的團隊
excerpt_en: Changing companies in direct selling is a leadership stress test. Strategic principles for moving without compromising integrity, breaking trust, or losing the tribe you've built.
excerpt_zh: 在直銷裡換公司，是一場領導力的壓力測試。如何在不犧牲誠信、不破壞信任、不失去你帶出來的人之下完成轉換。

title_en: The Mentor Trap: When Helping Too Much Hurts Your Team
title_zh: 導師陷阱：當過度幫助反而傷害你的團隊
excerpt_en: The most loyal mentors often build the most dependent teams. Why over-helping is a leadership failure disguised as generosity — and how to build true independence.
excerpt_zh: 最用心的導師，往往養出最依賴的團隊。過度幫忙其實是披著善意外衣的領導失敗，以及如何培養真正的獨立性。

title_en: When to Say No to a Prospect: The Hidden Cost of the Wrong Recruit
title_zh: 何時對準客戶說不：招錯人的隱性代價
excerpt_en: Not every lead is worth pursuing. The hidden costs of recruiting the wrong person — and when saying no is the most ethical, strategic move you can make.
excerpt_zh: 不是每個準客戶都值得追。招錯人的隱性代價，以及為什麼說「不」才是你最有策略的選擇。

title_en: The Smaller Market Advantage: Why 'Second-Tier' Cities Often Win Bigger
title_zh: 小市場的優勢：為什麼「二線」城市往往贏得更多
excerpt_en: Everyone chases Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Jakarta. But the smartest leaders are building in Ipoh, Kota Kinabalu, Surabaya. Here's why 'second-tier' cities quietly win.
excerpt_zh: 人人搶攻吉隆坡、曼谷、雅加達。但最聰明的領袖正在怡保、亞庇、泗水默默耕耘。這就是「二線」城市悄悄勝出的原因。

title_en: You Don't Need to Be a Salesman: Finding Your Ikigai in Direct Selling
title_zh: 你不需要當銷售員：在直銷中找到你的使命感
excerpt_en: The biggest myth in direct selling is that you need to be a natural salesperson. The truth is the opposite — the most successful people found their own unique path using the Ikigai framework.
excerpt_zh: 直銷最大的迷思就是你得天生會賣東西。事實正好相反，最成功的人透過Ikigai框架找到了屬於自己的獨特路徑。

title_en: Stop Pitching, Start Listening: The Art of the Follow-Up
title_zh: 停止推銷，開始傾聽：跟進的藝術
excerpt_en: Most leaders follow up by pitching again. The real art is listening — understanding what your prospect is actually thinking, and what they need to hear versus what you want to say.
excerpt_zh: 多數領袖的跟進就是再推銷一次。真正的藝術在於傾聽，理解準客戶心裡在想什麼，以及他們真正需要聽到什麼。

title_en: The Golden 72 Hours: What to Do the Moment Someone Joins Your Team
title_zh: 黃金72小時：新夥伴加入後你該做什麼
excerpt_en: The first 72 hours after someone joins your team are the most critical window. What happens in those hours determines whether they become a long-term builder or a 90-day dropout.
excerpt_zh: 新夥伴加入後的72小時是最關鍵的黃金窗口。這段時間的經歷，決定了他是長期經營者還是90天就消失。

title_en: The Alliance Problem: How to Build With Other Leaders Without Destroying Each Other
title_zh: 聯盟問題：如何與其他領袖共建而不互相拆台
excerpt_en: Crossline and peer-leader relationships are the most underestimated factor in long-term success. Learn the three toxic patterns — and how cooperative competition builds empires.
excerpt_zh: 旁線和同級領袖的關係是長期成功中最被低估的因素。認識三種有毒模式，以及良性競爭如何打造帝國。

title_en: The Terrain Has Changed: Why Yesterday's Playbook Is Losing You Tomorrow's Leaders
title_zh: 戰場已變：為什麼昨天的打法正在讓你失去明天的領袖
excerpt_en: The direct selling landscape has fundamentally shifted. Learn why yesterday's methods are losing you tomorrow's best leaders — and how to adapt without abandoning your principles.
excerpt_zh: 直銷的格局已經根本性地改變。看懂為什麼昨天的做法正在流失明天最優秀的人才，以及如何在不丟掉原則的前提下轉型。

title_en: The Passive Income Myth: What Direct Selling Really Pays You For
title_zh: 被動收入的迷思：直銷真正付你薪水的理由
excerpt_en: Passive income is the most overused promise in direct selling. Here is what the income actually pays you for — and why understanding this changes everything.
excerpt_zh: 被動收入是直銷中最被濫用的承諾。真正的收入到底在獎勵什麼？搞懂這件事，一切都會不同。

title_en: The 10-Year Test: How to Know If Your Direct Selling Career Will Last
title_zh: 十年大考：如何判斷你的直銷事業能不能走得長
excerpt_en: Most people think about their first 90 days in direct selling. Here is a framework of five questions to evaluate whether your approach will still be working a decade from now.
excerpt_zh: 多數人只想到直銷的頭90天。這裡有五個問題，幫你檢視自己的做法十年後還能不能站得住。

title_en: Stop Copying Your Upline: Why Duplication Is Killing Your Team
title_zh: 別再複製你的上線：為什麼複製正在扼殺你的團隊
excerpt_en: The industry loves the word 'duplication.' But blind copying is why most teams plateau. Learn the difference between duplicating principles and duplicating methods.
excerpt_zh: 這個行業最愛講「複製」。但盲目複製正是多數團隊卡住的原因。搞清楚複製「原則」和複製「方法」的差別。

title_en: The 5 Battles Every New Direct Selling Leader Must Win
title_zh: 新直銷領袖必打的五場仗
excerpt_en: The first two years are a battlefield. Most people who quit do so because they did not know which battles to fight. Here are the five that matter most.
excerpt_zh: 頭兩年就是戰場。多數人放棄是因為不知道該打哪些仗。以下是最關鍵的五場。

title_en: Why Your Team Keeps Quitting (And What You're Not Seeing)
title_zh: 為什麼你的團隊不斷離開（以及你沒看到的）
excerpt_en: If your team keeps leaving, the problem might not be them. Here are the three silent killers of retention that most leaders never see coming.
excerpt_zh: 如果你的團隊一直在流失，問題可能不在他們身上。這是多數領袖從未察覺的三大隱形殺手。

title_en: The General's Dilemma: When to Lead From the Front vs. From Behind
title_zh: 將軍的困境：何時衝前線 vs. 何時坐鎮後方
excerpt_en: When should you personally prospect, and when should you step back to develop others? The answer is a sliding scale, not a switch.
excerpt_zh: 什麼時候該親自上陣開發，什麼時候該退一步培養人？答案不是非黑即白，而是一把滑尺。

title_en: The Dual Perspective: What I Learned Moving From the Field to Management
title_zh: 雙重視角：從前線走到管理層的領悟
excerpt_en: Most direct selling trainers have only seen one side of the business. After 8 years in the field and 15 in corporate management, here is what both sides get wrong — and right.
excerpt_zh: 多數直銷培訓師只看過一面。走過8年前線和15年管理，以下是雙方各自的對與錯。

title_en: Why Most Network Marketing Leaders Are Busy, Not Strategic
title_zh: 為什麼多數網絡行銷領袖只是瞎忙，而非真正有策略
excerpt_en: You built the team. Revenue is growing. But somehow you are busier than ever. The problem is not your work ethic — it is your operating model.
excerpt_zh: 團隊建起來了，業績也在漲。但你卻比以前更忙。問題不在你的態度，而在你的運作模式。

title_en: Win the Right Way: Why Ethics Is Your Greatest Competitive Advantage
title_zh: 贏在正道：為什麼道德是你最大的競爭優勢
excerpt_en: In an industry where hype and shortcuts are common, ethical leadership is not just moral — it is the most powerful long-term strategy you can adopt.
excerpt_zh: 在一個充斥炒作和捷徑的行業裡，堅守道德不只是品格，更是你最強大的長期策略。
